title: Chronicle Release Manifest (Pipeline V1.2 / V2)
description: One file, two manifest shapes, selected by schemaVersion. schemaVersion 2 = a REPOSITORY release (kind pages | rollback | pipeline-admin), applied by pipeline/validate_and_apply.mjs and claimed by chronicle-release-gate.yml with {"kind":"pages"}. schemaVersion 3 = a WORKER release (kind worker), validated by pipeline/validate_worker_release.mjs and claimed by chronicle-worker-gate.yml with {"kind":"worker"}. The two never mix: each validator refuses the other's schemaVersion. This document is reference material - the validators are the authority, and they re-derive every digest, size and path rather than trusting a manifest's claim about itself.

repositoryRelease.title: Chronicle Release Manifest (Pipeline V1.1)
repositoryRelease.description: Chronicle Release Pipeline V1.1 manifest, schemaVersion 2. One manifest == one release == one commit on the target branch. schemaVersion 2 differs from V1's schemaVersion 1 in two load-bearing ways: (a) files[] no longer embed content - the bytes live in the D1 table release_payload as ordered base64 chunks, and each file carries only a payload descriptor; (b) the manifest carries manifestSha256 over its own canonical form. The gate re-derives every digest, size and path from the reassembled chunks and the working tree; it never trusts a manifest's claim about itself.

schemaVersion.description: Manifest schema version. Pipeline V1.1 accepts 2 only; a schemaVersion 1 manifest (inline content) is refused with exit 10.

manifestSha256.description: sha256 (hex) over the UTF-8 bytes of the canonical manifest JSON: all object keys sorted by code unit, arrays in order, no whitespace, and the manifestSha256 property itself removed before serialization. Verified by the gate; a mismatch is exit 19.

releaseId.description: Globally unique release identifier, format <YYYYMMDD>-<tag>. Uniqueness is enforced against git history via the 'Release-Id: <releaseId>' commit trailer (exit 18). A FAILed releaseId is quarantined in the queue and MUST NOT be retried; issue a new releaseId instead.

baseCommit.description: 40-hex commit sha the release was built against. MUST equal `git rev-parse HEAD` of the checked-out target branch at apply time (exit 11). This is the optimistic-concurrency token: if the branch moved since the build, the release is rejected and never retried.

commitMessage.description: Commit message. MUST end with the trailer 'Release-Id: <releaseId>'. The validator appends it when absent and rejects a different one (exit 10).

kind.description: pages = normal product release. rollback = a pages release restoring a previous state; requires rollbackOf. pipeline-admin = changes to .github/** or pipeline/**; the release-gate shim never hands one out, the gate validator refuses it, and it can only be applied by a human running pipeline/admin_apply.mjs.

rollbackOf.description: Required when kind=rollback: the releaseId being rolled back. Must differ from releaseId, and must be findable in the target branch history by its Release-Id: trailer. The validator enforces that the rollback RESTORES BYTES: each file afterSha256 must equal the blob recorded at commit(rollbackOf)^ for that path (exit 14), a path absent before that release must be deleted, and the set of non-Pages-trio paths must equal the set that release changed (exit 10). The Pages version trio is exempt from byte-exactness because pagesContract pins it to the rollback's own releaseId. See docs/V11_REAUDIT.md F2.

files.description: Complete, exhaustive set of file operations. After applying, `git status --porcelain` MUST describe exactly this set - no more, no less (exit 15).

limits.description: Declared limits. They may only be LOWER than the gate's hard caps (maxFiles 32, maxTotalBytes 4194304, maxFileBytes 1048576, maxChunkBytes 524288); a manifest cannot raise them. Effective limit = min(declared, hard cap). Violation = exit 17.

pagesContract.description: Static Pages deploy contract. Required for kind=pages and kind=rollback. version MUST equal releaseId. When checkBuiltMarkers is true the validator statically checks the version.txt / index.html BUILT / home.html HOME_BUILT trio (exit 16).

note.description: Free-form human note carried in the queue row. Not written to the repo.

path.description: Repo-relative POSIX path. Denied (exit 12): absolute paths, any '.' / '..' / empty segment, backslashes, control characters, leading/trailing whitespace, any '.git' segment, '.github/**', 'pipeline/**' except 'pipeline/PROBE.md' and 'pipeline/probes/<name>', and a basename of '.gitattributes' or '.gitmodules'. Also denied when the path or any of its existing parents is a symlink, or is recorded in the index with mode 120000.

beforeSha256.description: sha256 of the file bytes BEFORE the operation. null for operation=new. Checked against the working tree before applying (exit 13).

afterSha256.description: sha256 of the file bytes AFTER the operation. null for operation=delete. Checked after applying and again against the committed tree (exit 14).

size.description: Byte length of the file AFTER the operation; 0 for operation=delete. Must equal the real post-apply size (exit 14), and must not exceed maxFileBytes (exit 17).

payload.description: Descriptor for the chunked payload. Required for operation new/change; MUST be absent for operation=delete. The bytes themselves live in release_payload rows keyed (release_id, path, seq).

encoding.description: full-base64 = the reassembled payload is the complete post-operation file bytes (the only encoding allowed for operation=new). patch-base64 = the reassembled payload is a unified diff applied with `git apply -p1`; the diff MUST mention exactly one file whose a//b/ paths equal this entry's path (operation=change only).

payloadSha256.description: sha256 over the ENCODED payload, i.e. over the UTF-8 bytes of the full base64 text formed by concatenating every chunk_b64 in seq order. Mismatch = exit 19.

chunkCount.description: Number of release_payload rows for this (release_id, path). Their seq values MUST form the complete run 0..chunkCount-1 with no gaps and no duplicates (exit 19).

totalBytes.description: Byte length of the ENCODED payload, i.e. the sum of the lengths of every chunk_b64. NOT the decoded file size - that is `size`. Mismatch = exit 19.

workerRelease.title: Chronicle Worker Release Manifest (Pipeline V2, schemaVersion 3)
workerRelease.description: A worker release deploys exactly one Cloudflare Worker (novel-proxy) and touches no repository file. The payload is worker.js, carried as ordered base64 chunks in the same D1 table release_payload. Validated by pipeline/validate_worker_release.mjs, which re-derives every digest and renders the wrangler.toml the deploy uses. CRITICAL: a wrangler deploy uploads a new Worker VERSION, and a version carries its complete binding set - a binding the configuration does not declare is NOT in the new version. `bindings` is therefore mandatory and exact. Vars are preserved by keep_vars=true in the rendered config; secrets are never deleted by a deployment. See docs/PIPELINE_V2.md section 3.

manifestSha256.description: sha256 over the canonical manifest JSON (keys sorted by code unit, no whitespace, this field excluded).

targetWorker.description: Pinned in the validator. This gate deploys exactly one Worker.

expectedCurrentBuild.description: The workerBuild this release was built against. Compared with the LIVE root JSON before anything is deployed; a mismatch aborts (exit 20) because rollbackSha256 would no longer describe what is running.

newBuild.description: The workerBuild the new bytes report at GET /.

noop.description: REQUIRED true when expectedCurrentBuild == newBuild, and forbidden otherwise. An equal-build release is a probe: the post-deploy poll cannot distinguish a successful deploy from no deploy at all, so the release must declare that it knows this. Proof of landing is the version id in the wrangler deploy output.

workerSha256.description: sha256 of the reconstructed worker.js. Re-derived and compared (exit 14).

expectedEnvDelta.description: MUST be empty in V2.0. Any entry is refused (exit 21): this pipeline deploys code only. A release that needs a var, secret or binding change is an Owner dashboard action plus a separate code release.

rollbackSha256.description: The bytes to return to. For a no-op release this must equal workerSha256; for a build-changing release it must differ. A rollback is a NEW queued release carrying these bytes - never an automatic action.

rollbackBuild.description: Must equal expectedCurrentBuild: the state to roll back to IS the state this release replaces.

compatibilityDate.description: Pinned yyyy-mm-dd. Compatibility settings are part of a Worker version; letting wrangler default this would move the runtime under a bytes-only release. Owner-confirmed once.

compatibilityFlags.description: REQUIRED, and may be an EMPTY array. compatibility_flags is as much a part of a Worker version as compatibility_date: a flag that is live today and absent from the rendered wrangler.toml is switched off by the deploy. The field is required rather than defaulted to [] so that "no flags" is a statement the Owner made, not a value nobody supplied. Rendered into wrangler.toml always, including when empty.

bindings.description: Names and ids only. No secret value is ever carried in a manifest. The set must be EXACTLY the bindings novel-proxy uses: under-declaring removes a binding from the live Worker, over-declaring adds one nobody reviewed.

encoding.description: A Worker script is never patched; it is replaced whole.

limits.description: A manifest may declare LOWER limits but can never raise the gate hard caps.

then.description: a no-op release rolls back to the bytes it ships
